messages:
morgan: Quick sync — triaging audit logging coverage gaps across svc slices: api-gw, auth, console, billing, runtime. Need owners + backlog picks and quick validation plan for customer-facing audit events.

alexa: I can take api-gw. Noticed a few missing `request_id` and `principal_id` on 4xx flows, and some POST /v1/keys calls don't log KMS key refs.

kevin: I’ll own auth. There's a drift between RBAC changes and audit schema — role changes currently emit `user_role_update` but missing `actor_role` field. That breaks customer evidence exports.

jess: billing has spotty line-item ids in audit events for invoice adjustments. Customers want stable `resource_id` and `amount` fields for reconciliation.

sam: runtime (inference/runtime service) — KV cache hotpath drops trace_id on fast-path hits. Also need to ensure fallback model swaps are audited (model_id, previous_model, reason).

morgan: Good. Let's capture quick action items here. Also flag KMS integration questions: what metadata do we need in audit events for key usage vs key admin ops?

kevin: For KMS admin ops (rotate, grant, revoke) we should include `kms_key_id`, `operation`, `caller_principal`, `request_id`. For usage (encrypt/decrypt) include `kms_key_id`, `purpose`, and whether data_plane saw plaintext (boolean).

alexa: I'll add a sample audit schema snippet for api-gw 4xx + KMS tag so we can validate with customers.

alexa: ```json
{
  "event_type": "http_request",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-02T15:12:34Z",
  "service": "api-gateway",
  "request_id": "req_01F2...",
  "principal_id": "user:alice@example.com",
  "http": {"method":"POST","path":"/v1/models","status_code":403},
  "kms": {"kms_key_id":"key_123","operation":"encrypt","caller":"service:x"}
}
```

jess: Nice. We should also version the schema as `audit_event.v1` and add `schema_version` field in events so we can iterate without breaking customer exports.

sam: +1 on schema_version. Also propose we add a boolean `sensitive_data_redacted` for events where PII is scrubbed.

morgan: Ok owners and suggested schema changes noted. Now backlog triage: each owner to create a single ticket under SEC-AUDIT with checklist items: identify missing fields, add unit tests for event emission, update E2E export job, and provide sample customer payloads. Due EOD next Tue.

kevin: Creating SEC-AUDIT-778 now with the auth checklist and a short test harness for role change flows. @triage-bot please create link.

triage-bot: Created SEC-AUDIT-778: "auth: role-change audit schema fixes" — https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/SEC-AUDIT-778 :white_check_mark:

alexa: SEC-AUDIT-779 created for api-gw missing request_id + KMS metadata. Assigned to alexa.

jess: SEC-AUDIT-780 for billing adjustments audit enrichment created and assigned.

sam: SEC-AUDIT-781 for runtime trace_id and model-fallback audit events created.

morgan: Great. Two quick questions before we close: 1) Customer validation — do we want to publish a sample audit-event schema doc for customers to validate their ingestion? 2) Incident response: if we miss audit events during a rollout, what's the signal/alert?

kevin: 1) Yes. I can draft a short doc with sample JSONs and a validation script (python). 2) For alerts, we should add an SLO on audit event emission rate per critical endpoint and alert if emission < 99.9% over 10m. We already have metric `audit.events.emitted_total` tagged by `service` + `event_type`.

alexa: For validation script idea: simple Python check using JSON schema and sample payloads. Example snippet: ```python
from jsonschema import validate
# load schema v1
validate(instance=event, schema=schema_v1)
```

jess: Also add customer-facing checklist: required fields (request_id, principal_id, timestamp, service, event_type, schema_version). Put that in the doc.

morgan: I'll bundle the doc into the security docs space and link in the SEC-AUDIT tickets. Owners — please add PRs to your tickets and tag `eng-oncall` for rollback playbook review.

kevin: tagging security-bot to run a quick vuln triage if we touch RBAC code. @security-bot any special steps?

security-bot: Recommendation: add a pre-merge static scan for RBAC changes, run `snyk test` and a quick IAM policy lint, and include a short threat-model note in the PR. Also mark tickets as `vuln-sensitive` if they touch key management or auth flows.

morgan: Perfect. Final: owners + tickets recap — alexa SEC-AUDIT-779 (api-gw/KMS), kevin SEC-AUDIT-778 (auth/RBAC), jess SEC-AUDIT-780 (billing), sam SEC-AUDIT-781 (runtime). Due EOD Tue. I'll follow up in this thread with the doc link. Thanks :thumbsup:

alexa: Copy. Starting API audit tests now. :eyes:

kevin: Working on unit tests for role_change events.

jess: Will add sample customer payloads to the ticket.

sam: Adding runtime test harness and export validation.

morgan: Closing the triage — will post doc and escalate if any blocker shows up.

security-bot: Note: if any changes touch KMS key policies, please coordinate with infra and KMS-owner cadence to rotate keys safely.

morgan: Acknowledged. End of thread."
